title: What’s the right way to address your boss?
description:
Imagine you’ve just started a new job or it’s your first day at uni. You’re talking to your boss or teacher, someone who’s much older, much richer, or much more powerful than you. Do you call them by their first name? Or do you go with Mr, Mrs, Professor, Doctor?

In Nigeria, a video of a young woman being corrected for calling a billionaire businessman, Tony Elumelu, by his first name has sparked a conversation about respect, age and power.

We speak to three Nigerians to get their take on the story and how you should refer to your boss.

Plus our reporter Basma El Atti in Nairobi, Kenya, tells us about the unwritten rules elsewhere in the world.

summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores workplace hierarchy, respect, and naming conventions following a viral Nigerian video in which billionaire businessman Tony Elumelu corrected a young woman for addressing him by his first name. Presenter Hannah Gelbart discusses the clash between traditional respect for elders and modern Gen Z expectations with Nigerian guests, while BBC reporter Basma El Atti provides broader cultural perspectives from Kenya, Morocco, and the Arab world.
